title: Best credit cards for recurring bills and utilities in 2026
raw_text:
Everyone has recurring expenses, from rent or phone bills to simple utilities like gas or electricity. And unfortunately, paying for these expenses has left Americans feeling a financial pinch.
Fifty-six percent of Americans say everyday life has become less affordable for their household compared to one year ago, according to a CNBC and SurveyMonkey Quarterly Money Survey released in April, with 49% citing the rising prices of utilities and 32% citing rent or mortgage.
As such, wouldn't it be nice to earn rewards on those expenses? With the right credit card, you can — and for a $0 annual fee in most cases. Here, CNBC Select analyzed the five best credit cards for utilities and recurring bills, and how they can help you earn on monthly payments.
Best credit cards for recurring bills and utilities
- Best for paying home utilities: U.S. Bank Cash+® Visa Signature® Card
- Best for housing costs: Bilt Blue Card (see rates and fees)
- Best for streaming services: Blue Cash Preferred® Card from American Express
- Best for paying your phone bill: Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card
- Best for flat-rate cash back: Citi Double Cash® Credit Card
When should you use this card? If you have high home utility bills or are simply looking for a way to earn rewards on them, the U.S. Bank Cash+® Visa Signature® Card can help. The card earns 5% cash back on your first $2,000 in combined eligible purchases each quarter on two categories of your choice, one of which is home utilities. Provided your utilities don't exceed roughly $666 per month, you'll earn the full 5% on all your payments.
Other great perks: You'll also receive 2% cash back on one everyday category you choose each quarter, including grocery stores, gas and EV charging stations and restaurants. This card comes with a $0 annual fee and a reachable welcome bonus of $250 after spending $1,000 in eligible purchases within the first 90 days.
- Rewarding and versatile quarterly bonus categories
- Generous intro-APR offer
- Quarterly limits on the card's top bonus spending categories
- No statement credit offers or other ongoing benefits outside of the cash rewards
When should you use this card? If you pay rent or have a mortgage, the Bilt Blue Card will reward you for it. Earn up to 1X to 1.25X points on your rent or mortgage, depending on how you choose to earn your rewards. With a $0 annual fee (see rates and fees), if you spend enough on the card, you can essentially earn free points whenever you pay for housing.
Other great perks: The Blue Card is an entry point into the Bilt ecosystem, earning 1X points on everyday spending (non-housing purchases). Bilt Points themselves are very valuable, especially for travelers who can take advantage of their generous airline and hotel transfer partners. You also earn $100 in Bilt Cash upon approval.
The Bilt Blue Card offers a solid entry card to the world of Bilt, offering 1X on everyday purchases without charging an annual fee.

The category includes popular services like HBO Max, Hulu, Netflix, Peacock and 28 others. Plus, this card comes with statement credits toward select streaming services.
Other great perks: You'll also earn 6% cash back at U.S. supermarkets (up to $6,000 in spending per year). This card has a $0 annual fee for the first year; only in the second year does the (still reasonable) $95 annual fee start to apply.

When should you use this card? While the Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card doesn't offer direct rewards on your phone bill, you earn a flat 2% cash rewards on all purchases and up to $600 in cell phone protection against damage or theft (subject to a $25 deductible).
Other great perks: The Active Cash welcome bonus requires a very reasonable $500 in spending over the first three months to earn $200 in cash rewards. The card also offers a decent intro APR on both purchases and balance transfers, which could help if you're looking to reduce debt payments.
The Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card is great if you want simplicity thanks to its flat-rate 2% unlimited cash rewards on purchases and $0 annual fee.

Which is the best credit card for paying utility bills?
While it depends on the type of rewards you want, the U.S. Bank Cash+ earns 5% cash back on $2,000 in combined eligible purchases each quarter on two categories you choose (with utilities being an option).
Is it smart to put utility bills on a credit card?
It depends on how your utilities are billed. Many utility providers allow card payments but charge a fee, and if the fee is higher than your rewards, you'll lose money. It's also important that you're able to pay off your card each month, as credit card debt can be very costly.
Which Chase card is best for utilities?
The Chase Freedom Unlimited® (see rates and fees) is a top option for earning rewards on utilities. You'll earn an unlimited 1.5X on all purchases for no annual fee, and there's an easy-to-earn welcome bonus.
At CNBC Select, our mission is to provide our readers with high-quality service journalism and comprehensive consumer advice so they can make informed decisions with their money. Every credit card list review is based on rigorous reporting by our team of expert writers and editors with extensive knowledge of credit card products. While CNBC Select earns a commission from affiliate partners on many offers and links, we create all our content without input from our commercial team or any outside third parties, and we pride ourselves on our journalistic standards and ethics. See our methodology for more information on how we choose the best credit cards for recurring bills and utilities.
To determine which cards would best rewards users for recurring bills and utilities CNBC Select analyzed over 250 major credit cards issued by FDIC-insured banks and NCUA-insured credit unions.
We compared each card on a range of features, including the types of utilities or services covered, rewards (e.g., cash back, points and miles), annual fees, welcome bonuses, introductory and standard APR and balance transfer fees and foreign transaction fees.
We also considered additional perks (e.g., ongoing travel or merchant statement credits), cardholder protections (e.g., purchase protection, $0 liability protection and travel insurance), the application process when available (e.g., is there a credit pull or required credit score) and how easy it is to redeem points (e.g., are rewards are tied to a specific brand; if transferable, to how many/which partners, can you redeem for straight cash back).
When choosing the best credit cards for recurring bills and utilities, we focused on cards that offered elevated rewards on specific recurring billing categories (home utilities, housing payments, streaming services, phone bills, etc). We also incorporated 0% APR options, additional credits and bonuses provided by the card, and the number of categories each card might cover.
We also considered CNBC Select audience data when available, such as general demographics and engagement with our content and tools.
